newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count up 10 to 861 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count up 10 to 861 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 861 as of Nov. 27, up 10 from the prior week and 88 above the year-ago total of 773, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land rose by seven to 724, while rigs working offshore increased by one to 108. The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by two to 29.
The biggest change in individual states occurred in Texas, which showed an increase of 11 and Pennsylvania, which showed a decrease of three. Michigan rose by three.

A total of 382 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up eight from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas rose by two to 477, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs rose by eight to 349 versus 240 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 164 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Nov. 29, unchanged from the prior week.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 91.6 percent.
The number of working rigs in European/Mediterranean remained the same this week at 106 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 100 percent.
The worldwide rig count remained at 564 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 93.4 percent.
